utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just enlarge that. Now, on this map we have -- we've plotted where the bodies were found and either the names of the victims where known or an R number, which is the number the Serbian authorities gave them in 1998 during the exhumations. What I want to tell the Trial Chamber about now is the story of some of the bodies and how they got to be where they are, or where they were found, on that map. The first one I'm going to tell you about is that of Zenun Gashi, Misin Berisha, Sali Berisha, and 14-year-old Xhevat Berisha. That's counts 19 and 20 of the indictment. Now, Zenun Gashi was a Roma police officer on sick-leave since 1997 and recuperating from a heart attack. From his position, you can infer that he was not, and there will be evidence of this, a KLA sympathiser. He lived in Kosuric. On the 1st of August, 1998, KLA soldiers came to his home and unlawfully abducted him. They took him to the KLA headquarters in Rznic. He was detained there. Two other Roma people were there: Misin Berisha and his son Sali Berisha. The three were taken from Balaj's Rznic KLA headquarters to the site where their bodies were found. On about the 11th of September, 1998, the three bodies were found metres apart on the ground, next to the concrete wall. If you can just go into the shot of where their bodies were found. Each had multiple injuries - not that one, the photograph - and gun-shot wounds. Around Sali Berisha's neck was a mountain rope made into a noose. There was 2.5 metres of rusty barbed wire next to the bodies, and on one end of the bodies -- I'm sorry, and one end of the wire was tied into a noose. Long black hair and putrified soft tissue was caught in the barbs. Now, if you can see where the bodies were found, it's next to a site which I will show to you a little bit later, which was the -- which was an execution wall. You can see from a photograph of the skull of body R4, Zenun Gashi, if you look at the top photograph, you can see from the photograph there - that's just how his body was found - that he was shot through the head. There's a stick which shows the bullet trajectory right through. Xhevat Berisha, who was the 14-year-old son of Misin Berisha and the brother of Sali Berisha, went missing a little earlier in June or July 1998. Now, his body was found close by, about half a metre away from that of his father and his brother, Zenun Gashi near the execution wall. His skull, likewise, contained a bullet wound and his arms and legs had multiple fractures. An autopsy conducted in 19 -- in 2003, by international forensic experts, determined the cause of death to be a gun-shot wound to his head. His body contained multiple gun-shot wounds. The Defence does not dispute the identity of that particular body. Now, I want to take you to one of the photographs - it will come up in a moment - which shows the position of the bodies when they were -- when they were actually found. It flashed across the screen a moment ago and it shows the Serbian authorities in the process of -- in the process of exhuming the bodies. The bodies each were given markers. The markers you can see there on the screen. Kemal Gashi's body was marked 2; Misin Berisha marked 3; Zenun Gashi marked 4; and 14-year-old Xhevat Gashi marked 5. You can see where the people are. The person wearing the light blue and the gloves, just to the left of that was a wall which contained bullet-holes. We'll show you a little bit later a closer and better photograph of that. There was also an unidentified body, R1, which was underneath a body which is number 11 there, marked 11. Now, 11 - and this is important - was the mother of witness 4 who I will come to a little bit later. Body R12, which is also on that photograph, was discovered underneath the body of witness number 4. The next one I take you to is Idriz Hoti, which is counts 21 and 22. He was a 64-year-old Kosovar Albanian and an opposition party member, a member of the LDK. He disappeared in June or July of 1998 on his way to Jablanica, intending to join the KLA. His body was found underneath that of Misin Berisha you just saw, who was last seen at the detention in Jablanica in August of 1998, both were found at the execution wall. In other words, the body of someone who disappeared in -- or who was last seen in June or July 1998 was found underneath that of someone who was last seen actually in KLA custody in August of 1998. Now, next to his body, that's Hoti's, was a piece of black electrical cable similar to that found in the stables of the Ekonomija farm, which we have shown on the e-court. A 2003 autopsy by Professor Hoff-Olsen found a gun-shot wound to his head. The professor concluded that the probable cause of death was the gun-shot injury to the head and face. Likewise, for this body, the Defence does not dispute the body's identity. Counts 21 and 22, Velizar Stosic and Zdravko Radunovic. Velizar Stosic was a Serb who was last seen alive in July 1998 when he left his home in Belo Polje. His body, too, was found near the concrete wall. His skull, like others, contained wounds to both sides and his body contained multiple -- multiple fractures. A 2005 autopsy by international experts found the cause of death to him to be multiple gun-shot wounds to the head and legs. A tight noose made of a 1-centimetre-thick mountain rope was around his neck. A rifle projectile was next to his body. Now, the photograph which I'm just about to show, shows -- the middle photograph, shows a skull with a bullet wound to his head. Now, his body was found co-mingled with that of Zdravko Radunovic. Radunovic disappeared on the 18th of July, 1998. The significance of this is that Radunovic's wife will testify that the police told her that her husband was kidnapped by the KLA in Dujak village. His skull, likewise, contained a bullet wound. So we have two bodies together, both with one bullet wounds to the head and one of them of a person who was kidnapped by the KLA in July 1998. The Defence does not dispute the identity of either of these bodies. The next one is Pal Krasniqi, counts 31 and 32. Next to Radunovic's body was that of Pal Krasniqi. The significance of this is that he was last seen in the Jablanica KLA prison. Krasniqi was a Catholic Kosovar Albanian. On the 10th of July, 1998, he went to KLA headquarters in Jablanica - that's the headquarters run by the accused Brahimaj - to join up. Within days, however, a familiar accusation was made against him. He was denounced as a Serb spy for allegedly having a relationship with either a Serb or a Roma woman. The result of that information was that he was detained in the KLA custody at the Jablanica detention centre, the prison I showed you earlier. There he was beaten daily and brutalised with a baseball bat. His body, which was found in the picture which is shown on the screen now, contained multiple fractures to his arms which is consistent with the story of the beating with the baseball bat. Fluoroscopy examination in 2003 revealed a bullet core and its remains, there were gun-shot wounds on his head, trunk, and upper limbs. The cause of death was determined by international experts in 2003 to be multiple gun-shot wounds. The Defence, likewise, does not dispute that that is his body. The significance of my including him now is that he was a person last seen in custody of the KLA in Brahimaj's prison, was found next to the body of Radunovic, also said to have been kidnapped by the KLA, next to the body co-mingled of two people -- of another person who just disappeared. The next one is counts 21 and 22, and that is Nurije and Istref Krasniqi. They were an Albanian couple living in Turjak. A witness will testify that on about the 12th of July, 1998, KLA soldiers came to their home, and that a KLA commander ordered them to be taken to the KLA's headquarters in Glodjane. That was the accused Haradinaj's headquarters. The possible reason for this is that the couple had a good relationship with their Montenegrin neighbour -- with a Montenegrin neighbour which may have made them a collaborator in the eyes of the KLA. Now, their bodies were found together on the 12th of September, 1998, near the wall which -- near the execution wall. I'm just going to play you a very short portion of video taken by the Serb authorities on the 12th of September, 1998, which shows a close-up of the bullet-holes in the wall on the canal. As you can see, they're marked in blue. [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And number 14 and number 15 are Nurije and Istref Krasniqi's bodies. That's where they were found; you can see them in the video next to the shoes. Their bodies were found together on the 12th of September, the day the video was taken, right next to the wall containing the bullet-holes. Nurija's skull had fractures consistent with gun-shot wounds and his wife's body -- sorry, Istref's body was found close to his wife's. International forensic experts later determined the cause of death to be multiple gun-shot wounds to his chest. The next ones I take you to are two elderly Serb sisters, Vukosava Markovic and Darinka Markovic, that's counts 21 and 22. Vukosava Markovic was born in 1937 and Darinka Markovic was born in 1932. They lived in Gornji Ratis, which as you can see on the map is a very, very short distance from Rznic, Balaj's headquarters; in Glodjane, Haradinaj's headquarters. At the time of the disappearance between April and September 1998, they were the last remaining Serbs living in that particular village. Their bodies were found together next to the concrete canal wall, next to the execution site. The Defence disputes the identity of their bodies. Another body found next to the execution wall is that of Kemajl Gashi in counts 31 and 32. He was a Kosovo Albanian from Pec. Another familiar accusation was leveled against him. His son Medin joined the KLA in Baran in the summer of 1998. There, a KLA commander accused Kemajl Gashi, that's the older Gashi, of being a "Serbian spy." His son, who was in the -- sorry, who in the KLA, Baran headquarters, heard his father screaming from pain in the next room. He then saw his father the next day at the Baran headquarters. The significance of this is that Kemajl Gashi's body was found on the 11th of September, 1998, on the ground next to the execution wall near that of Misin Berisha. A 2003 autopsy, again by international experts, found fractures to his skull and multiple fractures to his body, which of course are consistent with the screams of pain which his son heard coming from the room. Gun-shot wounds to his pelvis may have caused his death. The Defence does not dispute that this is his body. Another one I take you to is the family of witness 4. From April 1998, armed KLA soldiers began harassing the family of witness 4 who lived in Donji Ratis. The KLA soldiers broke into their house; they searched for weapons; they threatened him. The accused Balaj himself personally participated often in these attacks. In about April or May 1998, KLA soldiers took witness 4's sister to the KLA headquarters - that's Balaj's headquarters - in Rznic. Balaj, in fact, escorted her home twice. However, like many others who went there, she has not been seen since. She hasn't been seen since the last time she returned to Balaj's headquarters. She's presumed dead, murdered by the KLA. Between the 10th and the 14th of August, 1998, Balaj and his KLA soldiers returned to witness 4's house and interrogated her mother. They took her away. A month later, on about the 11th of September, 1998, the mother's body was found next to the execution wall, next to an unidentified body. You can see on the photograph there how it was found next to the execution wall. That's the one that says "R11, mother of witness number 4." Professor Hoff -- sorry, it was found underneath an unidentified body. The unidentified body was subsequently labeled R1. The significance of this is that in 2003, an international forensic expert, Professor Hoff-Olsen, determined the cause of death to the unidentified body R1 as a gun-shot injury to the head. Witness 4's mother, found next to R1, who died from gun-shot wounds to the head, contained multiple gun-shot wounds to her pelvis. Dr. Marek Gasior, an international forensic expert, determined that the gun-shot wounds had caused witness 4's mother's death. The Defence doesn't contest that that body is that of witness 4's mother. Now, witness 4 had another sister, and sometime in late summer or early autumn 1998, Balaj and other KLA soldiers came to their house again in Donji Ratis. They kicked in the doors; they pointed rifles at the family, fired shots and abducted the second sister. You remember the first sister has disappeared without trace, and the mother was found dead next to the canal. A few days later, the body of the second sister was found in a forest about 20 kilometres from Donji Ratis. Her body had a bullet wound behind her ear, and her throat had been cut. Dr. Gasior, the international expert, in 2005, determined her cause of death to be multiple gun-shot wounds. The Defence does not contest that body found in the forest was witness 4's sister. About 13 bodies were found floating in the canal in the area below the concrete cascade shown in the photograph. In a moment on the screen, you will see the lower area of the canal which shows where -- which shows where other bodies were found. A mechanical engineer who worked on the water-supply to the lake will come to these chambers, and he will testify that the bodies could not have entered the canal from outside KLA-controlled territory. He will tell the Court how the canal was built in 1995. The canal contains about 35 and 40, or so, cascades. The water flows from an intake point in the village of Gornji, or upper Luka, which is several kilometres from Rznic. But the water passes through a series of steel grills, each of which is only about 5 centimetres wide. It also has large wooden gates and two sets of wooden filters, which are designed to stop things floating down the canal and into the lake. An object greater than 5 centimetres just could not have passed through the grills into the canal. In addition, the area in Gornji Luka was under KLA control between March and September 1998. But the area closest to where the bodies were found, between KLA-controlled Rznic and the execution site, in the relevant time of 1998 - can you please show that - was full of debris, large trees, sediment, old cars and rubbish. Just show the -- just come back. Right down the bottom, down here towards -- the area which is shown in the picture now, which is the very bottom of the picture, going all the way back towards Rznic, contain debris, large trees, sediment, old cars, and rubbish. And bodies just could not have floated from any other area to where they were found. They could only have been put in the canal from the point well inside the heart of KLA-controlled territory. As an example of the KLA control over that territory, one Serb witness will testify in the chamber that in late April 1998, he was arrested at the intersection of the road to Glodjane by about five armed KLA soldiers, who were concealing themselves under the concrete canal passing by the road. The next ones I take you to are counts 15 and 16, and that's Isuf Hoxha and Hajrullah Gashi. On about the 20th of July, 1998, they -- Isuf Hoxha, a Kosovar Albanian, and Hajrullah Gashi, a Kosovar Albanian - who made the mistake of being married to a Serb - were travelling on a bus from Djakovica to Pristina. On the road leading to Malisevo, which is close to Dulje, Haradinaj himself, that is the accused Haradinaj, and other KLA members, came onto the bus. Haradinaj said that he was looking for Hajrullah Gashi and Isuf Hoxha. Haradinaj and the KLA soldiers took the two men off the bus and put them in a black Golf, without licence plates, and drove them towards Glodjane. These two were last seen together in Haradinaj's custody on the way to his headquarters in Glodjane. Their bodies were found on the 12th of September, 1992, about 670 metres or so downstream from the end of the concrete wall near the water. The photograph I show you on the screen at the moment shows you the body of Hajrullah Gashi, as it was found by the Serbian authorities. The next one I take you to is that of Kujtim Imeraj, which is counts 21 and 22. About 10 metres from those bodies was the body of Kujtim Imeraj, who on the 4th of July, 1998, had been abducted by KLA soldiers under the command of Dervic Ukalj [phoen] who had come to his house in Selo. Again, a familiar accusation was levelled against him. He was accused of collaborating with the Serbs. The result of that was he was abducted, murdered, and his body was dumped by the canal. The next one is in counts 17 and 18. That's Illira Frrokaj. Illira Frrokaj was a Kosovar Albanian Catholic. She was stopped at a KLA check-point in Glodjane by Balaj himself and other KLA members in August 1998. Her body was found near her car, a red Opel, which the KLA had taken. The body was found burnt out and floating upside down in the canal. Her husband, Tush Frrokaj, who was with her when she was stopped at the check-point, has never been seen again. His body has not been recovered. Her body was found in the water a little way downstream from the KLA execution site. The body could only have been put there by the KLA in the area it controlled. Another unidentified body labeled R18I was found with her body in that canal. Another Serb couple, Milka and Milovan Vlahovic, that's counts 9 and 10 of the indictment, were a Serb couple living in Gornji Ratis. They remained -- they were elderly and they remained living there after the expulsion of -- or fleeing of all the other Serbs from the village in April 1998. Milka Vlahovic was born in 1933, and Milovan Vlahovic was born in 1935. They disappeared from the village in April 1998. In September 1998, Serb divers found part of Milovan's body in a riverlet in the natural part of the canal. They found some bones, which belonged to him, and a shoe. The degree of decomposition on the body was consistent with his death occurring between April and August 1998. The Defence does not dispute that it was -- the identity of the body. His wife, who has not been seen since 1998, her body has never been recovered. The Human Rights Watch report, which I referred to earlier, actually referred to the disappearance of this particular couple. The report said, and it's on the screen, in relation to Dar and Vukosava Markovic, Milka and Milovan Vlahovic: "According to both the Humanitarian Law Centre and Amnesty International, most ethnic Serbs fled their homes in Gornji Ratis on April 21 when the KLA took control of the village. Dar was 69; Vukosava was 65; and Milka was 62, and Milovan, 60, Vlahovic decided to stay, and their whereabouts are currently unknown." Well, as you've just heard, the update on the whereabouts of one of them is that the body was recovered in October -- in September 1998. Two other bodies were found. The body of Milka was the one that was recovered; the body of Milovan has not been seen since. I correct myself. Two bodies were found in a shallow grave at the junction of the roads leading to Dasinovac and Ratis. These were the bodies of Slobodan Radosevic and Milos Radunovic, two Serbs living in Dasinovac. What happened to them? What happened to them was that in the last week of April 1998, about ten KLA soldiers came to their house. Gunfire was heard and the soldiers rapidly left towards Decan. Their bodies were recovered in September 1998, and the photograph, which is about to be displayed, shows the bodies as they were found by the side of the road, with personal possessions. And forensic examination revealed that Slobodan Radosevic's skull contained a hole consistent with a bullet wound. Their disappearances, too, were noted in the Human Rights Watch report, which I referred to earlier. At page 83 of that report, it says: "Slobodan, 64, Milica 59, and Milos Radosevic, were the only ethnic Serbs to stay behind in Dasinovac when the UCK took control on April the 22nd." On September the 16 -- I'm sorry, I'll move to another one. Disappearances of people were presumed murdered, I take you to counts 23 and 24, which is that of Ivan Zaric, Agron Berisha and Burim Bejta. KLA soldiers abducted Ivan Zaric, a Serb; and Agron; and Burim Bejta while they were at the Granica mill. They were taken to Jablanica KLA headquarters and beaten. Brahimaj reported by radio to Haradinaj that the three had been captured. Haradinaj and Balaj then appeared at the headquarters, but the beatings conditioned. Later, while the men were serving food to the KLA commanders, including Haradinaj, Balaj himself mutilated the Serb boy's ear by severing it with a knife. Haradinaj sat there and continued to eat his dinner. Brahimaj said that "papers for Drenica would be issued." This was a euphemism for execution. Balaj led the three away. You will hear testimony that the three have never been seen again. They were last seen alive in the custody of the three accused. They are presumed murdered in KLA custody. That is the only inference available from a combination of all the evidence you will hear. Human Rights Watch reported on this incident in August 1998 in its report. It said: "Abductions of Roma. According to the Humanitarian Law Centre and the newspaper "Blic," Burim Bejta and Agron Berisha, both Roma; and Ivan Zaric, an ethnic Serb; left Dolac on May the 20th for the village of Grabanica. As of August 1998, their whereabouts were still unknown." There is no update on their whereabouts and the information about what has happened to them has come from witnesses that the Prosecution has interviewed since the Human Rights Watch report was issued. The finding of these bodies near the canal execution wall was no coincidence. Earlier I referred to ECMM monitors who went to the canal -- ECM monitors who were detained by Balaj and the KLA and released by Haradinaj in August 1998. They went to the canal area on the 18th of September, 1998. An independent monitor, who was an officer in an EU member state army, he's the one who was accused of being a Serbian spy, will testify in this court. He will testify that when he went there, "at the channel walls, one could clearly see the marks of bullets which had obviously killed these people." He was there during the exhumation of the bodies. If you see the clip of the video, you can see the bodies being recovered and you can see the bullet-holes just above the shovel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What you're watching now at the moment is a video taken by the Serbs -- Serbian authorities during the exhumation of the bodies in September 1998. The monitors saw the bodies; they were in an advanced stage of putrefaction. To that monitor who had been in the area and had been observing the clashes between the KLA and the MUP and the Serbian military, and who was aware who controlled what territory and when, it was clear to him that they had all been killed when the KLA controlled the area. He will testify in this court that there was no single Serb presence in the area until the Serbian attack, and that was at the end of August/beginning of September 1998. And that is entirely consistent with the evidence I have just led you to in relation to when people were last seen alive and when their bodies were recovered. Several hundred metres from these graves, as you can see on the large photograph, the large overhead photograph, was the Black Eagles' training ground at the Ekonomija farm. It was completely obvious -- it was completely obvious to the Black Eagles -- to the monitors, the ones who had been held hostage the previous month by the KLA, that the KLA controlled this area when the bodies were put there. And you can see on the map, which I've just shown in e-court, the Ekonomija farm is a very short distance from -- in the middle between the concrete canal where the bodies were found and the Glodjane headquarters and Haradinaj's house. And you can see the road leading from the KLA headquarters to the Ekonomija farm and the concrete canal. Skender Kuqi, counts 31 and 32, was a person whose body was not found at the execution site, nor at any location near the Lake Radonjic. He was a person who was murdered in KLA custody and died in hospital. He was a Kosovar Albanian from Zahac. Like many others, he was abducted by KLA soldiers. He was abducted around the 11th of July, 1998, and taken to the KLA headquarters in Jablanica. There, while in detention with Pal Krasniqi, whose body -- who I told you about earlier and whose body was found near the execution site, he was severely beaten with blunt instruments. He attempted at one point to escape the Jablanica prison with Mr. Krasniqi, but their attempt was unsuccessful. The KLA shot at them, they were recaptured, and returned to KLA custody. KLA members, including the two accused who sit in this court, Brahimaj and -- including the accused Brahimaj, severely beat him. Witness 12 will testify here. He will testify of a familiar accusation. He heard the accused Brahimaj accuse Kuqi of spying for the Serbs. That was an accusation familiar against -- sorry, a familiar accusation leveled against those whose bodies were later found battered and beaten. While in Jablanica detention, Skender Kuqi was beaten so severely by Brahimaj and other KLA soldiers that his body became swollen and he was unable to breathe because of his rib injuries. His kidney was exposed through his wound and his tongue began lolling from his mouth. He appeared dead, but Haradinaj, who was present, ordered that he be taken to hospital. This was in about July -- July the 16th, 1998. He died in hospital. Of the 13 bodies found in the water of the canal, eight had gun-shot wounds, often multiple, or fractures which were consistent with them being shot. All bodies had multiple fractures, none of that were consistent with that of a fall and other injuries which were inflicted before death. 18 bodies were found on the ground -- 18 to 20 were found on the ground near the concrete wall; 17 had gun-shot wounds, often multiple gun-shot wounds, and mostly to the skull, head, trunk, chest. Your Honours, the evidence of that is that their deaths -- the evidence of gun-shot wounds is entirely consistent with the execution by shooting at that wall. A further piece of forensic evidence is that spent cartridges were found there. Cartridges were found underneath the wall containing the bullet-holes where the bodies were found. A total of 124 spent bullet casings were found at three locations: Dasinovac, the Ekonomija farm, and Lake Radonjic. And I want to explain the significance of this. I'll take you back to the 24th of March, 1998. There was an altercation between the KLA and the MUP in the village of Dubravija. The MUP forces blockaded the area and managed to find some bullet casings. The Prosecution will produce a bullet report -- a ballistics report showing forensic analysis of the cartridges found at these locations showed identical patterns to cartridges found on the 24th of March, 1998, in Gramocelj when MUP units chased and captured two KLA soldiers. The accused are also charged under counts 35, 36, and 37 with rape, as persecution, as a crime against humanity and as a war crime. Witness 1 -- witnesses 1 and 2 lived in Rznic; they were not Kosovar Albanians. In either July or August 1998, Balaj came to their house with KLA soldiers and abducted them and took them to his nearby headquarters. Balaj threw witness 1 into a well, but he took witness 2, witness 1's wife, inside and interrogated her, the same accusation being leveled about allegedly collaborating with the Serbs. Witness 2 will testify in this court that he ordered the other soldiers to leave the room. He then, Balaj, repeatedly raped her. Another serious war crime charged is that of abduction, and I take you to counts 33 and 34. On about the 23rd of May, 1998, KLA soldiers abducted Kosovar Albanians Naser Lika and Fadil Fazlija, who were residents of Grabanica from the village of Zabelj. The accusation against them was one of treason. In their case, their crime was allegedly supporting the opposition, that is the Democratic League of Kosovo, the LDK. They were taken to KLA headquarters in Jablanica, that's Brahimaj's headquarters, where the three accused and other KLA members threatened them. Haradinaj himself told them that they couldn't live in Kosovo unless they helped to free the village from the Serbs. Later, in mid-July 1998 -- they were released. Later, in mid-July 1998, Brahimaj himself and other KLA members abducted Naser Lika from his home. They forced him into the trunk of a car, and they took Lika back to the headquarters in Jablanica. Haradinaj was present. Haradinaj personally ordered his men there to beat Lika, telling one KLA soldier named Bandash to "go ahead with your job," meaning to beat Lika. Bandash attacked Lika with a baseball bat, Balaj threatened him with death, and Haradinaj spat in his face. He was kept for three days in the water-soaked cellar in the Jablanica compound, which is now shown on the screen, and taken out regularly for beatings. The photograph on the screen, taken some years later, shows the basement filled with water, but witnesses will testify that it was in a similar -- similar condition at the time. Lika managed to escape after Brahimaj found that he could cook. He then employed him in the kitchen, and he managed to escape from there. The Jablanica detention centre was in operation from April till -- from April 1998 onwards. The KLA, under the control and direction of the three accused, established and operated this particular prison to detain, mistreat, and terrorise their perceived enemies; people who they perceived to be collaborators with the Serbian regime and opponents of the KLA. These were people such as Roma Kosovar, Catholic Kosovar Albanians, people who were particularly vulnerable to being labeled as a collaborator, a spy, or an enemy of the KLA. They were treated accordingly. The establishment and operation of this detention centre, the facility which is shown on the -- which is shown now, is entirely consistent with the KLA policy I've outlined, the policy under a joint criminal enterprise, of the campaign of fear against perceived KLA opponents in the Dukagjin Zone. It was entirely consistent with KLA-published policy. For example, in August 1998, the KLA actually declared in a public communique that "preventive measures are also being taken against certain collaborationist elements." Well, as I've outlined earlier today, you've heard the result of these preventative punitive measures being taken against the collaborative elements. They was so punitive and so preventive that the people could not do anything because they were dead. Although Haradinaj -- Brahimaj commanded the facility, Haradinaj visited regularly. And among the various KLA members involved in torturing prisoners there, Balaj was the most notorious for his cruelty.

utterances.text: The accused are also charged with a number of counts of deportation. Human rights monitors will testify in this court of their interviewing the members of terrified Serb civilian populations in around April 1998. They will testify that by May, the Dukagjin Zone KLA, under the control and command of Haradinaj, had largely achieved their goal. Using the tactics which I have outlined in my address this afternoon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, now the interpreters are the victims of you speeding up. I see that the French translation is already a couple of lines behind. So would you please try to finish in normal speed, in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will. Using the tactics which I have outlined in my address earlier this afternoon, they will describe how, by May 1998, the KLA, under the control of Haradinaj in the Dukagjin Zone, had largely achieved their goal, forcing all the Serbs out. The accused are charged with crimes against humanity. The test for crime against humanity is it has to be a widespread or a systematic attack upon a civilian population. From what I've described today, from the locations, the systematic nature of what happened, the areas in which -- the areas in which it occurred in the zone, the attack was widespread; it was systematic. As you can see from the shot on the screen, the yellow shows murder, the green shows detention, the red shows abduction, and the blue shows disappearance. This graphic, of itself, graphically illustrates where the attacks occurred against the civilian population. It was throughout the zone; it was a systematic attack; it was a coordinated attack; it was a deliberate attack. And having heard all of the evidence, the Trial Chamber will be in no doubt that the accused coordinated, participated in, and used others to direct this widespread or systematic attack against a civilian population in the Dukagjin Zone between March and September 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re. Before we take the break, Mr. Emmerson, is there any news as to whether or not Mr. Haradinaj would like to use an opportunity to give a statement under Rule 84 bis, as was unclear up till quite recently?
